clue.text: More than a hundred corrections to ignore

definitions.note: a hundred was an old subdivision of an English county; a region covers more ground

indicators.note: corrections rework something, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A long list of corrections that the reader is told to disregard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than a hundred' looks like a number, but a hundred was a historic division of an English shire, so a larger area fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundred was a small administrative district; a region is a wider area, more than one such district.

clue.text: A way to understand about Boatman, broadcast digitally

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

the setter, Boatman, refers to himself, so ME

explanation.surface: Someone describes how to make sense of the setter while it was sent out online.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by pseudonym, so 'Boatman' gives ME, here sitting inside READ.
explanation.definitionFit: Content that is streamed is transmitted over the internet as it plays, a form of digital broadcast.

clue.text: Perhaps Vincent de Paul, a priest in Gascony, brought up burps

explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' does double duty in the surface as a mild joke about burping, but it signals the reversal of ST + CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eructs is a formal verb for belching, bringing up wind from the stomach.

clue.text: Creates fresh draft from a hundred raw soldiers

indicators.note: the answer is taken out from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An officer draws up new plans using a hundred untrained recruits.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'hundred' through 'raw' to the start of 'soldiers'.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw a plan or design is to make a fresh version or new draft of it.

clue.text: Born romantic: a hundred music scores all begun by one composer

indicators.note: each of the preceding words starts with the letter wanted, so take every initial

explanation.surface: A romantic-era composer born to write a hundred musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms was a German Romantic composer, so he is one example of a composer.

clue.text: Perhaps ConservativeHome seized by slow type, heading for recession

indicators.note: the letters are captured and held inside the word for a sluggish person

explanation.surface: A Tory website is overtaken by a slow-moving writer as the economy declines.
explanation.walkthrough: ConservativeHome is a British political website; split, Conservative gives MP (an example of one) and Home gives IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something slumping is falling sharply, as an economy does on its way into a recession.

clue.text: Hundreds of runs etc — strangely, that's admitted

indicators.note: the abbreviation is let in, inside the rearranged letters
the letters are set out in an odd, unexpected order

parts.note: that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A cricket statistic: scores of a hundred runs and so on, oddly enough, conceded.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a century is a score of a hundred runs, so 'of runs' reads naturally with the definition, but 'runs' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A century is a group or score of one hundred, so the plural means hundreds.

clue.text: Amusing setter's latest splits party fifty-fifty

indicators.note: the letter breaks the party word into two parts

parts.note: a do is an informal party
the latest, or last, letter of setter
L is the Roman numeral fifty, twice

explanation.definitionFit: Droll describes a dry, quietly comic kind of humour, something amusing.

clue.text: A hundred to clue 4

explanation.surface: A cross-reference telling the solver that a hundred relates to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clue 4' looks like a pointer to 4 Down, but it is the result: the answer, read as five's core, yields the numeral for four.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so five scores make one hundred, an old way of counting.

clue.text: A hundred pence to embrace that fellow ape

indicators.note: the outer letters hug the pronoun between them

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
that fellow is him

explanation.surface: A pound coin offered to an ape to hug the fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimpanzee is one of the great apes, so chimp names an ape.

clue.text: Put briefly into boiling water, cutting out new cold tripe

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction about scalding tripe, minus the cold water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripe' looks like the ingredient being blanched, but here it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is slang for rubbish or nonsense talk, and blah is empty, meaningless chatter.

clue.text: Cartoons from Japan are funny; matinees not showing ET

these two letters are left out of the shuffled pool

parts.note: taken as written: E and T

explanation.surface: Japanese cartoons are amusing, and the afternoon screenings are not showing the Spielberg alien.
explanation.walkthrough: MATINEES without E and T leaves MAINES, which 'funny' rearranges; E.T. reads as the film but is just two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anime is the Japanese style of animated film and television, so animes are Japanese cartoons.

clue.text: Support for sources of fresh water? Hear, hear!

parts.note: wells are holes sunk to draw fresh water
aid means help or support

explanation.surface: A charity appeal for drinking-water wells, met with approval from the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Hear, hear' is the cry of agreement in Parliament, equivalent to applauding a speaker's good words.

clue.text: Resented being drugged inappropriately

indicators.note: done wrongly, so the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.definitionFit: If you grudged something you begrudged it, feeling resentment towards it.

clue.text: Trade uncovered over a hundred finalists in European space station

with its cover, the outer letters, taken off

indicators.note: the final letters of the following words

explanation.walkthrough: 'space station' reads as one thing, but 'space' gives its last letter and 'station' alone is the definition. Radio One is a BBC pop music radio station.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio 1 is the BBC's national pop music network, a broadcasting station.

clue.text: It's worth a hundred cents to escape from Monsieur Obrecht

indicators.note: the answer slips out from inside these two names

explanation.surface: A coin worth a dollar slipping away from a Frenchman named Obrecht.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Monsieur' into the start of 'Obrecht'.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro currency is divided into one hundred cents.

clue.text: See 23
Perhaps glass ceiling: no opening for job with old head of company at its core

explanation.walkthrough: 'no opening for job' plays on job vacancies, but it simply drops the J.

clue.text: Fan of austerity called out as an inflexible parasite

parts.note: an gives A; set means rigid or fixed; a tick is a blood-sucking parasite

explanation.surface: A supporter of spending cuts is denounced as a rigid freeloader.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic practises severe self-denial, so someone who embraces austerity of living.

clue.text: Retires with everyone's favourite vessels after every other raid

alternate letters, here the second and fourth

explanation.walkthrough: JO is the Scots word for a sweetheart, as in Burns's 'John Anderson, my jo'.
explanation.definitionFit: When a court or meeting adjourns, it breaks off and its members withdraw, retiring for a time.

clue.text: Showing pity for nothing: an empty hundred years, with no beginning and no end

explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses sympathy or dismay, the cry of someone showing pity or concern.

clue.text: Boatman told to go for being inattentive

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boatman' is the setter's own name, but here it means a sailor, AB.

clue.text: One hundred taken on by champion simultaneously

parts.note: an ace is an expert or champion

explanation.surface: A champion takes on a hundred challengers at the same time.
explanation.definitionFit: Done at once means done all together, at the same moment, so simultaneously.

clue.text: Good hundredth puzzle, accepted without debate?

explanation.walkthrough: The clue celebrates this being Boatman's hundredth Guardian puzzle; 'puzzle' looks like a noun but is the anagram verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure nodded through is approved by a committee or parliament as a formality, with no discussion.

clue.text: Lows include the core of a hundred states of mind

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lows' wants to mean depressions, fitting 'states of mind', but it is the cattle verb.

clue.text: Notes heartless move by way of working with African country, deporting the weak
